$comment: SURFACE-level read ledger. Sibling of docs/agent/review-coverage.json, and NOT the same thing: that one is FILE-level (which individual files a role opened, at what depth); this one is SURFACE-level (which package, directory or docs family has ever had a deep independent read run against it). The owner's worry on 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'only a select portion of the repo vs the full repo'. Validation is whole-repo on every push; the deep reads are chosen surface by surface, and nothing showed which surfaces had been chosen and which had never been looked at. A surface with an empty `reads` array has NOT BEEN READ, and that is the state this file exists to make visible rather than silent. GATED by scripts/check-surface-review-coverage.mjs: every tracked file must belong to a surface, every derived surface must have a row, every row's path must exist, and every read must carry a date (not in the future), a reviewer, a record and a scope. REPORTED, never fatal: how many surfaces are unread or partial, the oldest read, and staleness. SCOPE is required on every read and is the field that stops a slice counting as the whole: 'surface' means the whole surface was read; 'partial: <what>' names the slice and counts as PARTIAL; 'executed' means the surface was BUILT or RUN rather than read, and counts towards nothing. `open` and `closed` are the counts of findings the RECORD ITSELF names as left open / closed - transcribed from the record, not judged here. A row may also carry an optional `note`: one sentence for what an empty `reads` array cannot say on its own, usually that work landed NEAR a surface without being a read OF it. Optional, but never blank. A row says a read HAPPENED; the record is the only thing that proves it was any good.

reads.read: Fail-closed audit of the Zod validation surface (the whole runtime surface is one orval-generated file, api.ts, 355 lines; the 45 generated types are pure interfaces). Schemas are fail-closed by construction (no passthrough, no enum catch, coerce.date/number reject NaN). Systemic finding: the *Body/*QueryParams input schemas are DEAD as guards — the live /v1 routes hand-roll validation in v1.ts, which is itself fail-closed end-to-end (bounded TTL, bounded+refusing reconcile, core validateRequest rejects empty bindings). No live fail-open. Latent generated-schema tightenings + a dead-validator wiring gate filed to the backlog as design targets.

Adversarial fail-closed read of the audit-ledger surface (index/backend/types): canonical JSON sorts keys at every depth incl. inside arrays and escapes keys+values, depth-bounded (append refuses rather than hash a truncated form), secrets redacted before hashing; verifySegment field-set matches append; verifyLedger cap-honest, verifyLedgerFull paginates whole chain. backend appendWithChain atomic (advisory xact lock) so the chain can't fork; readiness asserts append-only (SELECT/INSERT/seq-USAGE required, UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE forbidden -> not ready), which is the structural tail-truncation defense. Zero fail-open/integrity defects; 2 non-defect notes (no external head anchor for admin-level tail truncation; substring secret-key match over-redacts).

Adversarial fail-closed audit of the cloud control plane (index.ts, 598 lines). Found and FIXED a real fail-open: bundle signature verification used a shared source-literal fallback key for any tenant absent from the signing registry, so a forged bundle for an unprovisioned tenant verified (golden rule 2 inverted on the authenticity boundary). Fix removes the fallback (signingKeyFor via hasOwnProperty -> undefined; verify fails closed; mint returns null), and adds a mutation-proven edge-sync-proof assertion (restoring the fallback -> 16/17 fail). Finding 2 (the proof could not catch it) fixed alongside. Finding 3 latent/deferred: empty-string tenantId resolves to a cross-tenant wildcard in five list methods (caller-gated today; follow-up to treat empty distinct from undefined). Rest verified fail-closed (checksum/signature guards, telemetry nonNeg, unknown->null, custodyGaps).

Follow-up (owner-requested): fixed Finding 3 from the control-plane read. Empty-string tenant/site scope in listSites/listEdgeNodes/listFleet/fleetHealth/operationalIntelligence resolved to a cross-tenant wildcard (`!tenantId`). Replaced with a scopeIncludes helper (undefined->all, empty/whitespace->none, else exact) and added 9 mutation-proven control-plane-proof assertions (restoring the old filter -> 40/42). No open findings remain on this surface.

reads.read: Adversarial fail-closed read of the DDM connector (index/apple-schema/fixture): deviceManaged is enrolled===true strictly; unknown/unreporting health and non-enforced binaryControl resolve to unknown/drifted; freshnessOf handles null/NaN/future (missing/unknown), and a malformed nowIso lands on expired via NaN-compare; enforcementCurrencyOf trusts only exact 'declarative' as current (legacy->dead/at_risk, unmapped->unknown); the `weak` OR can only raise assurance auto->step-up, never relax. apple-schema is a compile-time exhaustive provenance map. Zero fail-open defects; no material notes.

Adversarial read of the two-person normalizer/evaluator in the same sweep, confirmed by on-tree mutation. The authorizer normalizer's `!plain` and `readThrew` disjuncts were labelled 'genuinely inert' (a 239-shape behavioural diff) but are each the SOLE guard on one shape the diff never generated: a NULL authorizer body (hasUnrecognizedKey(null) never enters its walk) and a throwing accessor on a known key. Both are load-bearing; pinned with proof vectors, killed by the mutation guard, removed from the inert allowlist. Only the top-level twins are inert - now carrying an inert-at-top marker so the allowlist cannot launder the load-bearing terms.
